increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them test gaps rather than defects. What shipped: a collector-side lane join in store.getAgents behind GET /api/sessions/:id/agents, giving every span of a session a lane key of 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed' by resolving agent_id first and the parent-span chain second; a timeline module in argus-ui drawing one bar per lane over one shared window; and the six technical views (overview, todos, traces, events, metrics, raw) moved into a strip below the timeline, closed by default. npm --prefix tools/argus test 176 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 39 cases exit 0. Both correction rounds were spent because the visible behaviour was computed by a tested pure helper but never pinned in the rendered markup or the booted page; the round-2 fake-DOM harness in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs now boots public/app.js in-process, so later UI increments have a way to pin what the human sees.

increments.title: Activity and context growth drawn on each lane
increments.goal: Draw each lane's activity over time and, behind it, that agent's context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows its activity over time - tool calls and API requests - placed at the times they occurred, on the lane of the agent instance the activity belongs to.

Activity is assigned to lanes with the lane vocabulary the session's agents endpoint already serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed'), not a second attribution scheme; the records drawn here carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated.
Activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane rather than being dropped or folded into the main lane.
Each lane carries, as a curve or area behind that activity, the context size over time for that agent.

The curve is drawn from a size the telemetry actually records - the reported untruncated request-body length survives even when the body itself was truncated - and the view names which measure it is showing.
Growth in context size is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.
What proves this increment is the drawn result in the page: a change that stops the activity marks or the curve reaching the rendered timeline is caught, not only a computation checked in isolation.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: store.getAgents now joins claude_code.tool and claude_code.llm_request spans into a per-lane activity list and api_request_body records into a per-lane context series, both on the existing 'main' / 'agent:<agent_id>' / 'unattributed' lane keys; the content records carry no agent_id, so their lane is resolved through their spanId and a record whose span is unknown lands on unattributed, never on main; a requestBodyLength helper prefers the reported body_length over the delivered body, so a truncated or body_ref-only record still reports its true size; timeline.js draws an SVG area per lane scaled to one session-wide peak with activity ticks over it and a legend naming the measure; and app.test.mjs boots the real page and pins that marks and a non-empty polygon reach the rendered timeline. npm --prefix tools/argus test 186 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 54 cases exit 0. The fake-DOM harness plus the provability criterion cost this increment zero correction rounds, against two for the increment before it.

increments.title: Scrubbing the timeline, and a live mode that follows the head
increments.goal: Give the timeline a chosen time that can be moved to any point of the recorded session, plus a live mode that follows the newest data as it arrives.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session, and the chosen time is visible on the timeline.
The chosen time is drawn against the same shared window the lanes are already drawn against, so its position lines up with the activity marks and the context curve at that instant.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives, and keeps following as later data extends the session's window.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode.
A control returns to live mode.
The chosen time is one shared value the session view works from, so a later per-lane detail can be answered for exactly that moment.

What proves this increment is the behaviour of the page: a change that stops scrubbing moving the chosen time, or stops the live control returning to the head, is caught, not only a helper that maps a position to a time.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: state.atMs and state.following in app.js as the one chosen time the session view works from, chosenTimePct/clampChosenTime/laneRowsHtml/scrubStateHtml in timeline.js with a third options argument on timelineHtml, a playhead per lane placed by the same window arithmetic as the activity marks and the context curve, a range control that scrubs anywhere in the session, and a Live control that returns to the head; every refresh re-pins the chosen time to the head while following and only clamps a scrubbed time into the widened window. Two facts the next increment inherits: the scrub handler repaints the lanes and the readout in place through the ids timeline-lanes and timeline-scrub-state rather than re-rendering the detail, because a full render would destroy the range input mid-drag; and app.js's formatting helpers now live in public/format.js. npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 70 cases exit 0.

increments.title: Selecting a lane, and that agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Make a lane on the timeline selectable, and show for the selected lane the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each with its call parameters.
criteria: Selecting a lane on the timeline records a selection the session view holds beside the chosen time, and the selected lane is visibly marked on the timeline.
The lane selected is one of the lanes the timeline already draws, named by the lane vocabulary already in place (main, agent:<agent_id>, unattributed), not a second attribution scheme.
The selection shows the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each entry carrying the tool name and that call's parameters.

Whether the call parameters already arrive with the per-lane tool activity or have to be exposed for the first time is established and stated, and either way the panel reads them through the attribution already in place rather than joining records to agents a second way.

The listing is bounded by the selected lane and by the chosen time and follows the chosen time as it moves, so it never carries a call from after that moment; the scrub path repaints it in place, since a full re-render of the detail would destroy the range input mid-drag.

Which tools an agent used, and what for, is answerable for any lane the timeline draws at any point of the session, the unattributed lane included, and a lane with no tool calls before the chosen time says so.
With no lane selected the session view renders as it does today.

What proves this increment is the rendered page: a change that stops a lane selection reaching the panel, or leaves the panel showing the previous moment after the chosen time moves, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Split out of context-at-time after scrub-live. Scrub-live left the selection question untouched and added a constraint that lands squarely on this panel: scrubbing repaints the lanes in place through fixed ids instead of re-rendering the detail, so anything bound to the chosen time has to join that repaint path. That plumbing plus the selection mechanism is the load-bearing half of the old eleven-criterion increment and is worth its own review; it goes first because the context message list cannot be selected before a lane can be, and it delivers a whole acceptance criterion of the issue on its own.

return.summary: Add a selected lane to the session view and a panel that lists, for that lane, the tool calls up to the chosen time with their parameters, exposing the parameters for the first time on the existing per-lane activity entries of GET /api/sessions/:id/agents.

## The finding this increment turns on The call parameters do NOT arrive with the per-lane tool activity today; they have to be exposed for the first time. `store.getAgents()` builds each lane's `activity` entry as `{atMs, kind, name}` only (tools/argus/src/store.mjs, the span loop at ~line 995), where `name` is `attrs.tool_name` for a `claude_code.tool` span. The parameters live nowhere on that span: the CLI carries them on the `claude_code.tool_result` **log event**, in `tool_input` (JSON string, `tool_parameters` on CLIs before 2.1.x), which `toolParametersOf(attrs)` in tools/argus/src/claude.mjs already parses and which `store.mjs` already imports. `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` is on by default since the content-pipeline increment, so the attribute arrives. Expose them on the existing activity entry, through the lane attribution already in place — no second join from records to agents, no new endpoint. ## Collector: tools/argus/src/store.mjs, `getAgents()` 1. Add a module constant next to `MAX_LANE_ACTIVITY`: `const MAX_ACTIVITY_PARAMS_CHARS = 1000;` with a comment saying why it is capped (the payload is refetched on every coalesced ingest, and a single `Write` call's parameters are tens of kilobytes) and where the full text stays reachable (`GET /api/content?kind=tool_input&body=1`). 2. Give every activity entry a uniform shape: `{atMs, kind, name, params: null, paramsTruncated: false}`. `llm_request` entries keep `params: null` forever; only tool entries can gain params. 3. In the span loop, when a `SPAN.tool` entry is pushed and the span carries `attrs.tool_use_id`, register the pushed entry object in a local `Map` keyed by that id (`toolCallsByUseId`). Last registration wins for a repeated id; say so in a comment. 4. In the existing walk over `this.logs` (the one that builds the context curve), branch on `log.eventName` instead of `continue`-ing on everything that is not `EVENT.apiRequestBody`: keep the request-body arm exactly as it is, and add an arm for `EVENT.toolResult` that looks up `log.attrs?.tool_use_id` in `toolCallsByUseId`, reads `toolParametersOf(log.attrs)`, and — when both a matching entry and a parsed object exist — sets `entry.params = JSON.stringify(value)` truncated to `MAX_ACTIVITY_PARAMS_CHARS` with `entry.paramsTruncated = true` when it was longer. Do not add a second walk over `this.logs`: one scan is what the existing code costs and one is what it must keep costing. 5. A `tool_result` whose `tool_use_id` matches no tool span in the buffer adds nothing: no invented activity entry, no lane of its own. The mark comes from the span, so an unmatched result has no mark to decorate. 6. Ordering is already safe: the logs walk runs before the finalize loop that sorts and thins, and `thinEvenly` keeps the same objects, so an entry decorated in the logs walk is the entry that ships. 7. `params` is text, never a parsed object: a truncated JSON string is not valid JSON and nothing downstream may `JSON.parse` it. Rejected: attaching the parameters to a second per-lane list built by resolving `tool_result` logs to a lane through `log.spanId` — that is a second way of joining records to agents for data the span-derived activity entry already owns, and it would duplicate every tool call on the timeline. It must not throw on a lane with no `activity` key at all. 3. Export `laneDetailHtml(items = [], atMs = null, selectedLaneId = null)`. It returns `''` when `selectedLaneId` is null or matches no lane in `items` — that is what makes "no lane selected renders as it does today" true. Otherwise it returns a `

- C1 — the resting page. After `bootApp({...baseRoutes})`: `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML === ''`, the detail markup contains no `aria-current="true"` and no `tool-call` entry — with no lane selected the session view renders as it does today.
- C2 — a lane selection reaches the panel and the timeline. Fire `clickOn('[data-lane-id]', {dataset: {laneId: 'agent:agt-a'}})` on `detail`; then `laneRow(handle.el('detail').innerHTML, 'agent:agt-a')` contains `aria-current="true"` while `laneRow(…, 'main')` contains `aria-current="false"`, and the detail markup contains the tool name `Grep` and the params text `pattern` (assert on the escaped-safe substring `needle`, which survives escaping unchanged).
- C3 — the listing is bounded by the chosen time and follows it, repainted in place. Select `main` (its `Write` call is at `T0 + 9_000`, the chosen time starts at the head `T0 + 10_000`, so both calls are listed). Then fire `{target: {id: 'timeline-scrub', value: String(T0 + 5_000)}}` as an `input` on `detail`. Assert `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML` now contains `/early.md` and does not contain `/late.md`, and that `handle.el('detail').innerHTML` still contains `value="${T0 + 10_000}"` — the wholesale render did not run, which is what keeps the range input alive mid-drag. Then scrub back to `T0 + 9_500` and assert `/late.md` is in `lane-detail` again.
- C4 — the unattributed lane answers too. Select `unattributed`; the panel lists `Bash` and its `ls -la`.
- C5 — a lane with no tool calls before the chosen time says so. Select `agent:agt-b`; `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML` matches `/no tool calls/i` and contains no `tool-call-name`.
- C6 — the selection survives new data. Select `agent:agt-a`, then `handle.emit('ingest')` with a route function that moves `lastMs` (the shape the existing live-mode cases use), settle on the new `max=` reaching the detail markup, and assert the refreshed detail still marks `agent:agt-a` with `aria-current="true"` and still lists `Grep`.
- C7 — clicking the selected lane closes the panel again. Select `agent:agt-a`, fire the same click a second time, and assert `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML === ''` and no `aria-current="true"` anywhere in the detail markup.
- C8 — switching sessions drops the selection. Select `agent:agt-a`, then click `[data-session]` for `sess-2`, settle on `agent:agt-c` reaching the page, and assert `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML === ''`. (`agentsTwo` has no `activity` key at all, so this also pins that the old payload shape does not throw on the selection path.)

Not covered here on purpose: mouse-drag ergonomics and focus restoration (the harness has no real DOM), keyboard activation of the lane row (it is a real `<button>`, so the platform owns it), and pixel appearance of the selected-lane marking.

increments.title: The selected lane's context at the chosen time as a structured message list
increments.goal: Show, in the panel the lane selection already opens, the selected agent's or the main session's context as of the chosen time, rendered as a message list whose blocks collapse to one line with a size and expand to the exact text.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent's - or the main session's - context as of that moment, in the same panel the selection already opens.
The context shown is the body of the nearest API request at or before the chosen time on the selected lane, chosen by the lane vocabulary already in place.
It is rendered as a structured message list distinguishing system prompt, user, assistant, tool call and tool result blocks.
Each block is collapsed to one line carrying its size.
Each block expands to the exact full text the record carries, and a body the CLI truncated is marked as truncated instead of being presented as the whole context.
A record that reports a body length but carries no body text at all is shown as its reported size with the text stated to be absent, rather than as an empty context.
A lane with no API request at or before the chosen time says so, rather than showing another lane's context or the nearest later one.
Moving the chosen time moves the context shown, and the context and the tool listing in the panel agree about lane and time bound at every moment.

What proves this increment is the rendered panel: a change that stops the context reaching the panel, or stops an expanded block showing the full text, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Kept its id and kept last, but reduced to the context half: the selection mechanism and the tool listing moved to lane-select, so nothing is built twice. The earlier merge of tools-at-time assumed the tool list would come second and repeat the selection work; putting the selection in the increment before it removes that reason. What stays here is the part the run still knows least about - the shape of a request body and what a truncated or text-free record can be rendered as - which is why it is worth its own research-test-build-review chain rather than eleven criteria in one.

increments.title: The selected agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, the tools that agent has used up to that moment together with the parameters of each call.
increments.note: Dropped as its own increment and never revived under this id. Its criteria were folded into context-at-time after content-pipeline showed tool parameters arrive as the same content records as request bodies and lane-activity put each lane tool calls, with names and times, on the /agents payload; after scrub-live they moved on into lane-select, which now carries the selection plus the tool listing while context-at-time carries the context. The work happens, under those two ids.

increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them test gaps rather than defects. What shipped: a collector-side lane join in store.getAgents behind GET /api/sessions/:id/agents, giving every span of a session a lane key of 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed' by resolving agent_id first and the parent-span chain second; a timeline module in argus-ui drawing one bar per lane over one shared window; and the six technical views (overview, todos, traces, events, metrics, raw) moved into a strip below the timeline, closed by default. npm --prefix tools/argus test 176 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 39 cases exit 0. Both correction rounds were spent because the visible behaviour was computed by a tested pure helper but never pinned in the rendered markup or the booted page; the round-2 fake-DOM harness in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs now boots public/app.js in-process, so later UI increments have a way to pin what the human sees.

increments.title: Activity and context growth drawn on each lane
increments.goal: Draw each lane's activity over time and, behind it, that agent's context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows its activity over time - tool calls and API requests - placed at the times they occurred, on the lane of the agent instance the activity belongs to.

Activity is assigned to lanes with the lane vocabulary the session's agents endpoint already serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed'), not a second attribution scheme; the records drawn here carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated.
Activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane rather than being dropped or folded into the main lane.
Each lane carries, as a curve or area behind that activity, the context size over time for that agent.

The curve is drawn from a size the telemetry actually records - the reported untruncated request-body length survives even when the body itself was truncated - and the view names which measure it is showing.
Growth in context size is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.
What proves this increment is the drawn result in the page: a change that stops the activity marks or the curve reaching the rendered timeline is caught, not only a computation checked in isolation.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: store.getAgents now joins claude_code.tool and claude_code.llm_request spans into a per-lane activity list and api_request_body records into a per-lane context series, both on the existing 'main' / 'agent:<agent_id>' / 'unattributed' lane keys; the content records carry no agent_id, so their lane is resolved through their spanId and a record whose span is unknown lands on unattributed, never on main; a requestBodyLength helper prefers the reported body_length over the delivered body, so a truncated or body_ref-only record still reports its true size; timeline.js draws an SVG area per lane scaled to one session-wide peak with activity ticks over it and a legend naming the measure; and app.test.mjs boots the real page and pins that marks and a non-empty polygon reach the rendered timeline. npm --prefix tools/argus test 186 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 54 cases exit 0. The fake-DOM harness plus the provability criterion cost this increment zero correction rounds, against two for the increment before it.

increments.title: Scrubbing the timeline, and a live mode that follows the head
increments.goal: Give the timeline a chosen time that can be moved to any point of the recorded session, plus a live mode that follows the newest data as it arrives.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session, and the chosen time is visible on the timeline.
The chosen time is drawn against the same shared window the lanes are already drawn against, so its position lines up with the activity marks and the context curve at that instant.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives, and keeps following as later data extends the session's window.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode.
A control returns to live mode.
The chosen time is one shared value the session view works from, so a later per-lane detail can be answered for exactly that moment.

What proves this increment is the behaviour of the page: a change that stops scrubbing moving the chosen time, or stops the live control returning to the head, is caught, not only a helper that maps a position to a time.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: state.atMs and state.following in app.js as the one chosen time the session view works from, chosenTimePct/clampChosenTime/laneRowsHtml/scrubStateHtml in timeline.js with a third options argument on timelineHtml, a playhead per lane placed by the same window arithmetic as the activity marks and the context curve, a range control that scrubs anywhere in the session, and a Live control that returns to the head; every refresh re-pins the chosen time to the head while following and only clamps a scrubbed time into the widened window. Two facts the next increment inherits: the scrub handler repaints the lanes and the readout in place through the ids timeline-lanes and timeline-scrub-state rather than re-rendering the detail, because a full render would destroy the range input mid-drag; and app.js's formatting helpers now live in public/format.js. npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 70 cases exit 0.

increments.title: Selecting a lane, and that agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Make a lane on the timeline selectable, and show for the selected lane the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each with its call parameters.
criteria: Selecting a lane on the timeline records a selection the session view holds beside the chosen time, and the selected lane is visibly marked on the timeline.
The lane selected is one of the lanes the timeline already draws, named by the lane vocabulary already in place (main, agent:<agent_id>, unattributed), not a second attribution scheme.
The selection shows the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each entry carrying the tool name and that call's parameters.

Whether the call parameters already arrive with the per-lane tool activity or have to be exposed for the first time is established and stated, and either way the panel reads them through the attribution already in place rather than joining records to agents a second way.

The listing is bounded by the selected lane and by the chosen time and follows the chosen time as it moves, so it never carries a call from after that moment; the scrub path repaints it in place, since a full re-render of the detail would destroy the range input mid-drag.

Which tools an agent used, and what for, is answerable for any lane the timeline draws at any point of the session, the unattributed lane included, and a lane with no tool calls before the chosen time says so.
With no lane selected the session view renders as it does today.

What proves this increment is the rendered page: a change that stops a lane selection reaching the panel, or leaves the panel showing the previous moment after the chosen time moves, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Split out of context-at-time after scrub-live. Scrub-live left the selection question untouched and added a constraint that lands squarely on this panel: scrubbing repaints the lanes in place through fixed ids instead of re-rendering the detail, so anything bound to the chosen time has to join that repaint path. That plumbing plus the selection mechanism is the load-bearing half of the old eleven-criterion increment and is worth its own review; it goes first because the context message list cannot be selected before a lane can be, and it delivers a whole acceptance criterion of the issue on its own.

increments.title: The selected lane's context at the chosen time as a structured message list
increments.goal: Show, in the panel the lane selection already opens, the selected agent's or the main session's context as of the chosen time, rendered as a message list whose blocks collapse to one line with a size and expand to the exact text.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent's - or the main session's - context as of that moment, in the same panel the selection already opens.
The context shown is the body of the nearest API request at or before the chosen time on the selected lane, chosen by the lane vocabulary already in place.
It is rendered as a structured message list distinguishing system prompt, user, assistant, tool call and tool result blocks.
Each block is collapsed to one line carrying its size.
Each block expands to the exact full text the record carries, and a body the CLI truncated is marked as truncated instead of being presented as the whole context.
A record that reports a body length but carries no body text at all is shown as its reported size with the text stated to be absent, rather than as an empty context.
A lane with no API request at or before the chosen time says so, rather than showing another lane's context or the nearest later one.
Moving the chosen time moves the context shown, and the context and the tool listing in the panel agree about lane and time bound at every moment.

What proves this increment is the rendered panel: a change that stops the context reaching the panel, or stops an expanded block showing the full text, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Kept its id and kept last, but reduced to the context half: the selection mechanism and the tool listing moved to lane-select, so nothing is built twice. The earlier merge of tools-at-time assumed the tool list would come second and repeat the selection work; putting the selection in the increment before it removes that reason. What stays here is the part the run still knows least about - the shape of a request body and what a truncated or text-free record can be rendered as - which is why it is worth its own research-test-build-review chain rather than eleven criteria in one.

increments.title: The selected agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, the tools that agent has used up to that moment together with the parameters of each call.
increments.note: Dropped as its own increment and never revived under this id. Its criteria were folded into context-at-time after content-pipeline showed tool parameters arrive as the same content records as request bodies and lane-activity put each lane tool calls, with names and times, on the /agents payload; after scrub-live they moved on into lane-select, which now carries the selection plus the tool listing while context-at-time carries the context. The work happens, under those two ids.

return.summary: Closed scrub-live as done (review accepted, no findings, one round) and split the last open increment in two. The only substantive change to the open cut: context-at-time carried eleven criteria covering three distinct jobs - a lane selection mechanism, a tool listing per lane and time, and a structured expandable context message list - which is the largest remaining piece of the issue and larger than any increment worked so far. It is now lane-select (selection plus the tool use up to the chosen time) followed by context-at-time (the context message list in the panel that selection opens). Criteria stay disjoint: the issue bullet on tool use per agent and per time is lane-select's alone, the bullet on the context as a structured message list is context-at-time's alone, and no criterion sits in both. Selection goes first because nothing can be shown for a lane before a lane can be picked, and because scrub-live added a constraint that lands on exactly that plumbing - the scrub handler repaints the lanes and readout in place through fixed ids rather than re-rendering the detail, so any panel bound to the chosen time must join that path or go stale mid-drag; lane-select now names that as a criterion. Context-at-time keeps the part the run knows least about (request body shape, truncated bodies, records that report a length but carry no text) so that risk gets its own review round instead of sharing one. Rejected: keeping the merged eleven-criterion increment, since four of eight increments are spent and two remain spare after this split; and re-splitting the way the earlier merge feared, where the tool list would come second and repeat the selection work - putting selection in the first half removes that objection. The stale note on the dropped tools-at-time was updated to point at both successors. No questions: nothing in the remaining cut turns on a decision only a human can make, and the open data question (whether tool call parameters already reach the /agents payload or must be exposed) is written into lane-select for the researcher to answer first.
